text:
Marco Chen: Heads-up — HermesFinance handed off their private/VPC sizing ask. They want a prod pod that can handle normal steady traffic ~120 RPS (avg short chats, ~40 tokens) with a 5x seasonal spike window for 3 weeks. Also must support burst-to-hosted fallback and keep egress < 2 TB/day for EU region.
Anya Patel: thanks — do we have their model profile? quantized 8-bit Llama2-13B or 4-bit? that changes GPU RAM and throughput.
Marco Chen: baseline is rlhf-finetuned Llama2-13B-quant8. They want deterministic latency p95 < 250ms for single-turn chat when not bursting.
Devon Lee: quick numbers: Llama2-13B quant8 on A100-ish gives ~350 tokens/sec per ~GPU for generation-only with small context. But with chat and 40 tokens avg ~= 0.11 sec per request if fully isolated.
Junaid Qureshi: want the math. If steady 120 RPS and each request is 40 tokens => 120 * 40 = 4800 tokens/sec. If one GPU does 350 tok/s, needed GPUs = ceil(4800/350) ~= 14 GPUs. Add 30% headroom for concurrency spikes and KV-cache IO => 18 GPUs.
Olivia (solutions): Hermes explicitly asked for cold-start safety and a canary policy to fall back to hosted. Can we recommend a dedicated min-pool + burst credits config?
Marco Chen: proposal: min-reserved pool = 18 GPUs, burst pool = 6 GPUs (short-lived), autoscale target to 24 GPUs. That covers sustained 5x spike? check: 5x tokens => 24000 tok/s. 24 GPUs * 350 = 8400 tok/s — not enough. We need a different strategy.
Anya Patel: right — full 5x is unrealistic to cover with just GPUs. Options: 1) queue/ingest throttling, 2) graceful degrade to smaller model (7B quant4) for burst, 3) hosted fallback to serve overflow. Mix is typical.
Devon Lee: do a hybrid plan: reserved 18 GPUs for steady, 8 GPUs for intra-VPC burst, and a routed overflow to hosted with routing policy that prefers local until queue > 250ms. For 5x we assume 3x local + 2x hosted. Calculate capacity: local supply = (18+8)*350 = 9100 tok/s ~ covers ~1.9x steady; hosted covers rest.
Junaid Qureshi: egress calc: avg tokens -> payload + metadata. Assume 1 token ~ 4 bytes compressed across websocket chunking. For their steady 4800 tok/s => ~19KB/s => 1.6GB/day; for 5x spikes offloaded to hosted the egress could spike but capped by routing. We must cap to 2 TB/day — seems fine if majority stays cached.
Olivia (solutions): include recommended HW SKUs and network: suggest 18 x A100-40GB or 18 x H100-80GB if customer wants headroom for larger context. If they choose H100, we can reduce GPUs to ~12 because H100 throughput ~2x for our kernel set. But cost delta is big — list both.
Marco Chen: config snippet for runbook and headroom calc (quick):
```
# headroom calc (approx)
steady_tok_s = 120 * 40
gpu_tok_s = 350  # a100-40GB baseline
needed_gpus = ceil(steady_tok_s / gpu_tok_s)
reserved = needed_gpus * 1.3  # 30% headroom
burst_pool = min(8, reserved*0.4)
```
sre-bot: Incident note created for this sizing thread: INC-2024-HE-001 (for network egress constraints). +1
Anya Patel: network notes — EU customers need private peering and we should recommend colocated NAT or egress gateways to control daily caps. Suggest BGP route filtering + per-subnet rate limiting at the VPC edge.
Devon Lee: ops runbook items: warm-up plan for KV cache: add scheduled prefix warmers hitting top 500 user prompts over 6-minute rolling windows during expected peak ramp. That reduces token cost by ~20% on average.
Olivia (solutions): I'll convert this to a one-pager for Hermes with 2 options: (A) cost-optimized: H100 small pool + hosted overflow, (B) reliability-first: larger A100 fleet with more local burst. Include estimated GPU-hours/month and ballpark cost ranges.
Marco Chen: action items:
- @Anya finalize H100 vs A100 perf numbers and update GPU counts (ETA 24h)
- @Devon draft runbook warming script and autoscaler policy (ETA 48h)
- @Olivia prepare customer one-pager with cost brackets and fallback policy (ETA 72h)
- @Junaid validate egress cap assumptions with network team and add NAT sizing (ETA 48h)

Marco Chen: ping if anyone sees a fatal flaw. Otherwise I'll slot a follow-up sync with Hermes on Thursday.
